judgment_contract.additional_judgments: Post-output review belongs in a separate exploratory artifact bound to fixture and output hashes. It cannot rewrite frozen qrels or qualify further tuning as independent.
judgment_contract.anchor_match: Match exact repository-relative path and indexed symbol name. <module> anchors are predeclared only when the module directly owns the requested operation; file co-location alone is not relevance.
judgment_contract.anchor_recall_at_k: Retrieved unique listed relevant anchors divided by listed relevant anchors; sparse anchor recall does not claim completeness over repository relevance.
judgment_contract.hit_at_k: Every planned positive query remains in the denominator. A frozen relevant anchor among the first k emitted rows is a useful entry-point hit. Failed executions remain unknown, not empty and not successful.
judgment_contract.judged_precision_at_k: Listed relevant rows divided by listed relevant plus explicit-distractor rows. Retain returned, judged and unjudged counts; unlisted rows are unjudged, not automatically irrelevant. Undefined with no judged result.
judgment_contract.negative_queries: expect_empty is a diagnostic of the complete unsupported requested operation. Lexical candidates are not evidence the capability exists; errors remain errors.
judgment_contract.reporting: Retain full output and emitted rank order; show planned and successful execution denominators and distinguish module from function/method anchors.

provenance.aggregate_context_disclosed: Root disclosed that previous sets were spent and the general ranking principle was changing. The author received no new policy implementation or per-query results.
provenance.source_basis: Same immutable tracked-working-tree source snapshot after owned parser/grant rustdoc and before ranking edits. Exact source-file SHA256 bindings identify judgment inputs; HEAD alone is insufficient for dirty source.

purpose: Final small qualification set of new positive owners for a retrieval policy fixed before this run.

selection.independence: Same author, same repository and purposive selection. This is blindness to the current policy and its outputs, not independence of author, codebase or task taxonomy. Earlier related workflow concepts exist, so no cross-family or population novelty claim is made.
selection.input_contract: Queries use at most twelve plain whitespace words, avoid mixed-case identifiers and stay within 256 UTF-8 bytes. Validation does not claim the serving tokenizer is equivalent to whitespace splitting.
selection.limitations: Small purposive local sample with sparse labels. No random sampling, human ground truth, user-query-frequency estimate, population relevance inference or semantic answer-quality conclusion. The set is spent for independent claims after outputs are inspected.
selection.method: Selected eight real operations from runtime owners not previously used as positive owners. Read source contracts in the immutable snapshot and authored queries and sparse labels before viewing the corrected policy or output. Three negatives request new unsupported operations/domains.
selection.qualification_use: Single final qualification. If a change fails this set, its outputs may explain rejection but must not become a tuning loop presented as an independent pass.
selection.split_note: Previously exposed regression; source bindings refreshed only.

source_rebinding.purpose: spent regression only; query/anchor/distractor judgments unchanged
